svg.title: Direct Lake Internals: Residency, Transcoding, and Fallback
svg.desc: An internals diagram starting at a query hitting a Direct Lake model in one of four residency states: cold, semiwarm, warm, or hot, with latency improving at each step. A cold query triggers transcoding, remapping Parquet row-group dictionaries into a single global VertiPaq dictionary — a process whose cost is set by the table's row-group count, mapped one-to-one onto VertiPaq column segments. A framing node shows how a metadata-only refresh resets which Delta commit the model reads from and can evict segments; a companion node lists the three eviction triggers. A decision node forks by storage flavor: Direct Lake on SQL can fall back to DirectQuery under three documented triggers, while Direct Lake on OneLake never falls back at all. Two warning nodes cover the Overwrite-defeats-incremental-framing trap and the SQL-view-forces-fallback trap.
svg.text: Direct Lake — Lazy Loading, Framing & Fallback Internals

g.title: Query hits a residency state — A Direct Lake model sits in one of four memory-residency states, with latency improving at each step.
g.text: Column residency lifecycle · cold-query transcoding · framing/eviction triggers · DirectQuery fallback decision (Direct Lake on SQL only)

svg.text: LANE 1 — COLUMN MEMORY-RESIDENCY STATES (latency improves left → right)

g.title: Cold query: transcoding — Direct Lake merges per-row-group local Parquet dictionaries into a single global VertiPaq dictionary.
Row-group-to-segment mapping — Row groups map one-to-one to VertiPaq segments; sizing them right is the real performance lever.
g.text: LANE 2 — TRANSCODING GRANULARITY: ROW GROUPS MAP 1:1 TO VERTIPAQ SEGMENTS

svg.text: 1 row group → 1 VertiPaq column segment (1:1 mapping)
Many small row groups → many small segments → slower queries
Avoid: row groups well under 1M rows
~1 GB BinSize target · partition only on
no stats-based skipping used by loader

g.title: Framing — A metadata-only refresh that rebinds the model to the current Delta commit's file set.
g.text: LANE 3 — FRAMING (WHEN THE MODEL RE-BINDS TO DELTA) & COLUMN EVICTION

svg.text: Evict only segments of removed row

g.title: Trap: Overwrite defeats incremental framing — Loading with Overwrite wipes commit history, forcing a full cold reload on the next query.

svg.text: not live table — writes after it are invisible
get consistent results during long loads
Parquet files in one Delta table
3 reasons a resident column is evicted

g.title: Eviction triggers — Refresh, non-use, or memory pressure can evict a resident column back to cold.

svg.text: Anti-pattern: vacuuming the Parquet files of the currently framed commit version breaks user queries until the next reframe

g.title: Which Direct Lake flavor? — DirectQuery fallback exists only in Direct Lake on SQL; Direct Lake on OneLake never falls back.
g.text: LANE 4 — DIRECTQUERY FALLBACK DECISION (root cause: which Direct Lake flavor is this model?)

g.aria-label: Trap: SQL view silently forces fallback
g.title: Trap: SQL view silently forces fallback — A model table based on a SQL view forces every query into DirectQuery fallback.
DirectQuery fallback (SQL flavor only) — Three documented triggers force a query to bypass Direct Lake and read the SQL endpoint directly.
g.text: On fallback: query reads the SQL endpoint directly

svg.text: Returns latest data (escapes the framing point-in-time) — typically slower than Direct Lake
XMLA fingerprint: compatibilityLevel ≥ 1604, partition mode = directLake,
partitions reference a shared expression as their data source
